newsitem.title: UK: YACHTING-UK SAILOR WHO RESCUED RIVAL GETS HERO'S WELCOME.
newsitem.headline: YACHTING-UK SAILOR WHO RESCUED RIVAL GETS HERO'S WELCOME.

text.p: British round the world yachtsman Pete Goss arrived home on Saturday to a hero's welcome for abandoning the race to rescue a French rival midway through the voyage.

Six Royal Marine trumpeters sounded a fanfare as Goss's yacht entered Plymouth harbour on Britain's south coast accompanied by an armada of small boats and tugs, and some 5,000 people turned out to cheer the local sailor.

Last weekend an estimated 150,000 people cheered Goss into the French port Le Sables D'Olonne. France has awarded him one of its highest civilian honours, the Legion d'Honneur, for abandoning his chances of winning the race by going to the rescue of stricken 25-year-old French racer Raphael Dinelli, whose yacht had capsized about 1,000 miles (1,600 km) south of Australia.
"Life comes first. It is a rule of the sea. We all have to help each other," Goss told reporters on Saturday.
After the rescue Goss had to carry out surgery on his own infected elbow after receiving instructions by satellite.
Goss ended the Vendee Globe race fifth out of six finishers. After rescuing Dinelli, he had to restart the 22,000-mile race from Tasmania but was credited with the time taken up with the rescue.
